title: tool-calling SFT re-run with the fixed checkpoint saver -- and what selection actually says
why: Every prior SFT run wrote identical weights to every checkpoint (upstream-asks entry 8), so best-checkpoint selection was impossible. This is the first SFT run in this project whose checkpoints differ, and the first time the selection question can be asked at all.

run.note: identical to the published stage-2 configuration except save/eval density and the saver

checkpoints_genuinely_differ: step_250 vs step_500:   0/66 identical, max abs diff 1.562500e-02
step_1250 vs step_3000: 0/66 identical, max abs diff 3.906250e-02
step_250 vs step_3000:  0/66 identical, max abs diff 4.687500e-02
divergence grows with step distance; prior runs were 66/66 identical at max abs diff 0.0

paired_schema_valid_3000_minus_1250.unit: question (8 questions x 8 samples; the completion is NOT the exchangeable unit)
paired_schema_valid_3000_minus_1250.verdict: SUGGESTIVE, NOT SIGNIFICANT -- t=2.55 is below this eval's declared CRITICAL_T of 2.843 and the sign test gives p=0.125. n=8 questions is underpowered. What is NOT in doubt is the DIRECTION: the best-val checkpoint is not better, and is most likely worse, on the task gates.

finding_validation_loss_is_the_wrong_sel: Val loss bottoms at step 1250 and rises to 3000, while schema validity RISES over the same span (0.7344 -> 0.8906) and parse rate with it (0.7812 -> 0.9219). The mechanism is in the split, not the model: stratified_split holds out an even share per category and there are exactly two categories (tool_calling, base_blend), so ~50 of the 100 val examples are base-blend. Half the validation loss is plain language modelling with no bearing on tool-call format adherence, so minimising it optimises partly for the wrong thing. Selection for this objective should use the task gate on dense checkpoints -- which this saver fix makes possible for the first time -- not the val curve.
correction_to_the_overfitting_claim: CLAUDE.md previously recorded that 'both tool-calling runs overfit' because val rose monotonically after step 1000, and treated evaluating an earlier checkpoint as the natural remedy. Rising val did not mean the task got worse here; it got better. 'Overfit' was inferred from a proxy that does not track the objective.

quantified_cost_of_the_saver_bug.reading: The published runs shipped their step-1000 weights whatever the filename said, and scored 0.75. This run's step_1250 -- the nearest comparable weights -- scores 0.7344, and its real step_3000 scores 0.8906. The within-run comparison is paired and the cross-run one is not (different run instances), but both point the same way: the saver bug was discarding the last two-thirds of every SFT run. Suggestive, and one seed; a seed replicate is what would settle the size of it.

limitations: One seed (5489), one run per arm. No seed replicate.
n=8 questions is the binding constraint on power, not the 8 samples per question.
The cross-run comparison against the published stage-1/stage-2 numbers is unpaired.
Only two checkpoints of the twelve were evaluated on the gates (best-val and final); the full 12-point gate curve was not measured.
